land.text: the Mark Brandenburg under the Hohenzollern, with the Altmark, without the pawned Neumark and the Międzyrzecz castellany; 'On 20 March 1414, the Brandenburg estates swore allegiance at Tangermünde'; Frederick was 'recognized as margrave and elector at the Council of Constance' in 1415

successors.note: The same state (same Wikipedia article and Wikidata Q148499): the existing electorate-of-brandenburg dossier starts in 1415 and names this one as predecessor. They should be one colour; this dossier could not absorb that one because it belongs to another batch.

capitals.name: Brandenburg an der Havel
capitals.note: Infobox 'Brandenburg an der Havel (1157-1417), then Berlin (1417-1806)'. 'Charles IV chose Tangermünde as the electoral residence' (page, undated, Luxembourg period 1373-1415); not entered as a capital because the infobox keeps Brandenburg an der Havel. The gazetteer lacks the name; coordinates are the town's.

keyframe_review.note: 30.2 k km2 (33.6 k by the grid) for 1260-1271, from the Altmark to the Oder; the page does not say how far the Mark reached east in 1260. Dated pieces: 'in 1252 the Margraviate of Brandenburg and the Archbishopric of Magdeburg purchased the Lubusz Land', Landsberg founded 1257, 'The Templars sold Soldin to the Ascanians in 1261'. Landsberg lies about 20 km beyond this outline's east edge (15.0 E); left as a soft frontier. The Margraviate page's only area figure is about 26,000 km2 'by 1535', not usable for 1260. Repair 2026-10-25: verdict changed to adjust for 1260-1261 only. Upper Lusatia (Budissin Land) is added from 1262 (Upper Lusatia page: the Ascanian margraves attained it 'Between the death of King Wenceslaus I of Bohemia in 1253 and 1262'; Cliopatria draws none of it).

correction.text: the 1260 outline unchanged, for 1260-1261 only; Upper Lusatia is added from 1262 by the next keyframe
the 1260 outline plus Upper Lusatia (Budissin Land, with Bautzen and Görlitz), for 1262-1271

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1262-1271 (repair): the 1260 outline plus Upper Lusatia, which the Ascanian margraves held by 1262 (the page's window for the acquisition is 1253-1262, so they may already have held it in 1260-1261) and lost in 1319. In 1268 Otto IV divided it into the countries of Bautzen and Görlitz. No Cliopatria shape draws it; the region name 'Upper Lusatia' is not yet in the gazetteer.

correction.text: the 1272 outline (Mark plus Neumark east of the Oder) without the Deutsch Krone strip, which the page says Brandenburg annexed in 1296, plus Upper Lusatia; for 1272-1295 only

keyframe_review.note: 41.5 k km2. The outline reaches 16.9 E and 54.0 N and already contains Deutsch Krone and the lands north-east of it. 'Brandenburg annexed the Międzyrzecz castellany from Greater Poland in 1297, and Deutsch Krone in 1296'; 'In the late 13th century, the margraves conquered northwestern parts of Greater Poland'. The strip is removed to 1295; it is lost again in 1368 ('Otto lost Deutsch Krone to Casimir the Great'). The Neumark pages date no other step, so the rest of the 1272 outline stands. Repair: Upper Lusatia added (held 1262-1318). The German Neumark (Landschaft) page dates the north-eastern Neumark in steps: Arnswalde 'vor 1269', the Zantoch castellany 1270, Berlinchen 1278, Schivelbein 'um 1292', Dramburg 1297, so the single 1272 step is Cliopatria's; Arnswalde, Berlinchen and Dramburg cells are inside the 1272 outline and are left as drawn (soft).

correction.text: the 1272 outline with Deutsch Krone, annexed in 1296, plus Upper Lusatia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1296-1304: the 1272 outline as Cliopatria draws it, with the Deutsch Krone strip restored from 1296 ('Deutsch Krone in 1296'). Upper Lusatia added in the repair.

correction.text: the 1305 outline plus Lower Lusatia and Upper Lusatia, for 1305-1313

keyframe_review.note: 41.7 k km2, 3 cells (the Międzyrzecz castellany, annexed 1297) more than 1272, and 'in 1303 it [Lower Lusatia] was acquired by the Ascanian margraves of Brandenburg', which no Cliopatria shape of this row draws. The Waldemar page instead has 'Frederick of Meissen had to cede the March of Lusatia as well as the towns of Torgau and Großenhain to Brandenburg' in 1312; the 1303 date is used. Upper Lusatia (held 1262-1318) is added as well. The outline holds to 1313; the next Cliopatria shape starts in 1314.

correction.text: the 1314 outline plus Lower Lusatia and Upper Lusatia, for 1314-1318

keyframe_review.note: 44.1 k km2. The 10 cells the 1314 outline adds to 1305 (14.7-15.5 E, 52.1-52.4 N) are Rzepin, Torzym, Sulęcin, Międzyrzecz and one cell by Schwiebus; Züllichau (15.6 E) is in no outline. The Margraviate page treats Torzym Land and Sulęcin as Brandenburg's Lubusz Land until the 1319-1322 interregnum, so the outline stands from 1314 (the first version of this dossier moved it to 1319; withdrawn after the review). 'In 1319 Waldemar acquired the Silesian towns of Züllichau and Schwiebus' (Waldemar page) is drawn as a 20 km disc from 1319 (next keyframe). The Waldemar page also says the margrave 'had to surrender Stargard and Neubrandenburg to Mecklenburg' and waive Schlawe and Stolp by the 1317 Treaty of Templin; those are ledger events, but no Cliopatria outline holds the land.

correction.text: the 1314 outline plus the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the New March that Wartislaw IV took; Lower and Upper Lusatia are gone, for 1319

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1319 (repair): the Ascanian line has died out. Out for this year: Lower Lusatia (south to Jawor, north to Saxe-Wittenberg after the siege of Gubin), Upper Lusatia (west to Bohemia, east to Jawor) and the New March ('In 1319, Wartislaw IV of Pomerania took control of the New March with Torzym Land'). In: the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc. The Torzym-Sulęcin cells stay in until Jawor's 1320 portion. Henry II of Mecklenburg, Rudolf I of Saxe-Wittenberg and Otto the Mild of Brunswick-Lüneburg also took parts of the margraviate that year; the page's regions for them are not entered and the Mark west of the Oder is left whole.

correction.text: as 1319 and also without the Torzym-Sulęcin cells of the Lubusz Land, which passed to Henry I of Jawor, for 1320-1321

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1320-1321 (repair): 'a large portion of the Lubusz Land passed to Duke Henry I of Jawor' in 1320. The page names no towns for Jawor's portion; the eight Rzepin-Torzym-Sulęcin cells of the 1314 delta stand for it (reading).

correction.text: as 1320 and also without the Międzyrzecz castellany, held by Henry IV of Żagań by February 1322 and not returned, for 1322-1323

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1322-1323 (repair): the Międzyrzecz castellany (the three cells of 1297 plus the Międzyrzecz town cell) is out for good: 'ultimately reintegrated with Poland'. In 1323 Louis IV grants Brandenburg to his son.

correction.text: as 1322 and with northern Lower Lusatia back, for 1324-1325

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1324-1325 (repair): 'In 1324, the northern part passed to the House of Wittelsbach' (Lower Lusatia page). The New March and the Torzym-Sulęcin cells stay out until the 1326 bridge.

correction.text: Brandenburg without the Wittelsbach lands of Bavaria that Cliopatria draws into the row, with the Altmark, northern Lower Lusatia and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany, for 1326-1332

keyframe_review.note: 77.8 k km2 is not the Mark alone: take out Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria outline of 1305 (Upper Bavaria with the Palatinates, 148 cells, bbox 7.1-12.7 E) and what is left is the 1314 outline (44.1 k) less six cells of the central Altmark (11.2-12.3 E, 52.5-52.7 N: Stendal and Tangermünde), which are added back. The Louis IV page gives his Upper Bavarian reign as 1301 to 1347 (infobox) and 'In 1323 Louis gave Brandenburg as a fiefdom to his eldest son Louis V'; the Margraviate page: in 1351 Louis I gave the Mark to his half-brothers 'in exchange for Upper Bavaria'. Bavaria is therefore taken out; the duchy-of-bavaria dossier draws it as its own 1326-1328 keyframe. Lower Lusatia: 'In 1324, the northern part passed to the House of Wittelsbach' (Lower Lusatia page). Repair: the Międzyrzecz castellany is removed (1322), the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added (1319); the New March and the Torzym-Sulęcin cells are back from this year (1326 bridge, confidence 1: no page dates the recovery).

correction.text: Brandenburg without Bavaria, with the Altmark, northern Lower Lusatia and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany, for 1333-1343

keyframe_review.note: 80.4 k km2 = Cliopatria's Bavaria outline of 1450 (Upper and Lower Bavaria, 36.7 k, bbox 10.1-13.7 E) plus the 1314 outline less 8 Altmark cells and plus 9 cells south-east of Berlin (13.2-14.7 E, 52.0-52.5 N: the Storkow-Beeskow side, also in the later outlines, which no page opened explains). Louis IV held Upper Bavaria from 1301 and inherited Lower Bavaria only in 1340 ('With the death of duke John I in 1340 Louis inherited Lower Bavaria'), so even as a Wittelsbach union the shape is early; Bavaria is taken out for the duchy-of-bavaria dossier. Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added. The 9 'new' cells south-east of Berlin (13.2-14.7 E, 52.0-52.5 N) stay unexplained: a grid probe puts neither the Storkow nor the Beeskow town cell in any outline, so the Storkow page ('Storkow passed to the Lands of the Bohemian Crown in 1367, together with Lower Lusatia'; merged into the electorate in 1571) does not bear on them.

correction.text: Brandenburg without Bavaria, with the Altmark, northern Lower Lusatia and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany, for 1344-1351

keyframe_review.note: 80.5 k km2, the same lump (+0.1 k; 8 Altmark cells missing, 8 cells south-east of Berlin added). Tyrol (1342) and Holland (1345) are not in the outline and are the Bavarian and Dutch dossiers' business. 'In 1351, Louis I gave the Mark to his half-brothers Louis II (the Roman) and Otto V, in exchange for Upper Bavaria' (Margraviate page). Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added.

correction.text: the Mark as in 1314-1351 with northern Lower Lusatia and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany, under Louis II (the Roman) and Otto V

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1352-1367: Cliopatria has no Margraviate shape for 1352-1384 (the Mark lies inside its Duchy of Bavaria row, which holds 187-189 of the 196 cells of the 1314 outline). Electorate from 25 December 1356; 'In 1367, Otto sold Lower Lusatia to Charles IV'. Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added.

correction.text: the Mark after the loss of Lower Lusatia (1367) and Deutsch Krone (1368), with the Altmark that the 1385 outline omits and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1368-1384: 'In 1368, Otto lost Deutsch Krone to Casimir the Great'; 'In 1373, Charles IV bought Brandenburg from Otto for 500,000 guilders.' The 1385 outline is the nearest Cliopatria shape; it carries the same Altmark gap (below). Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added.

correction.text: the 1385 outline plus the Altmark and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany

keyframe_review.note: 42.1 k km2. The outline has no Stendal, Tangermünde or Gardelegen cell (all three are inside the 1314 outline), yet 'Charles IV chose Tangermünde as the electoral residence'. The Altmark is therefore added back. The outline also gains 9 cells south-east of Berlin (Beeskow side) that the 1314 outline lacks; the page does not date or explain them, so they stand. The page's only area figure is about 26,000 km2 'by 1535'. Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added.

correction.text: the 1395 outline plus the Altmark and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany

keyframe_review.note: 41.9 k km2, one cell more than 1385; nothing on the page changes in 1395. Altmark added for the reason given at 1385. Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added.

correction.text: the 1402 outline without the whole Neumark, plus the Altmark and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany

keyframe_review.note: 35.6 k km2: the outline drops 7.3 k km2 in the north-east (Arnswalde, Dramburg, Schivelbein) but keeps Landsberg, Küstrin and Soldin, which are the Neumark's heart, while 'Brandenburg pawned the Neumark to the Teutonic Knights in 1402' and the Order 'passed completely under their control in 1429'. The whole Neumark is removed. The existing electorate-of-brandenburg dossier believes the Neumark is wholly absent from these shapes; the grid says otherwise. Page figure 'about 26,000 km2 by 1535' against 35.6 k: ratio 0.73, inside a factor of two, but not the same year. Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added.

correction.text: the 1407 outline without the whole Neumark, plus the Altmark and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the Międzyrzecz castellany, for 1407-1414

keyframe_review.note: 35.6 k km2, identical to 1402. In 1411 Frederick of Nuremberg 'was granted hereditary control over Brandenburg'; on 20 March 1414 the estates swore allegiance to him at Tangermünde; the Neumark stays pawned to the Order (1402-1454/1455). Repair: Międzyrzecz castellany removed, Züllichau-Schwiebus disc added.

region.text: the Mark Brandenburg from the Altmark to the Oder under the Ascanian margraves

ledger.note: 1260: the Ascanian Margraviate of Brandenburg enters the map. Infobox 'Established: 3 October 1157'; 'Around 1250, the margraves took Lubusz Land from a fragmented Poland.' The margraviate is older than Cliopatria's row, which starts here; the page gives no boundary.

region.text: Soldin (Myślibórz) in the Neumark

ledger.note: 1261: the Ascanians buy Soldin. 'The Templars sold Soldin to the Ascanians in 1261.'

region.text: Upper Lusatia (Budissin Land: Bautzen, later Görlitz, Zittau and Lubań)

ledger.note: 1262: the Ascanian margraves hold Upper Lusatia. The page: 'the Ascanian margraves of Brandenburg attained Budissin Land' 'Between the death of King Wenceslaus I of Bohemia in 1253 and 1262'; 'Neither the exact date of the acquisition nor the legal form of ownership' can be established (feud, marriage or pledge). Dated to the end of the window, so Brandenburg may already have held it in 1260-1261; Bohemia as counterpart is my reading of the sentence (the page names no seller). In 1268 Margrave Otto IV divided it into the countries of Bautzen and Görlitz. In no Cliopatria outline.

region.text: the Neumark east of the Oder that Cliopatria's 1272 outline adds: Landsberg (founded 1257), 'extended eastward to the Drawa and north to the Parsęta through purchases, marriage pacts, and service to the Piast dynasty'; the cells inside Cliopatria's Greater Poland shape of 1271

ledger.note: 1272: Cliopatria's outline adds the Neumark east of the Oder (53 cells, 13.4 k km2): 35 of them lie inside its Duchy of Greater Poland shape of 1271, 17 inside its Holy Roman Empire Minor States shape (the West Pomeranian side, which that dossier books as its own loss, see the next event), one in neither; this event takes the Greater Poland side and the odd cell. No page gives 1272. The German Neumark (Landschaft) page shows a gradual acquisition: 'Lebus 1249 bis 1287', Arnswalde 'vor 1269', the Zantoch castellany 1270 (previous holder not named), Berlinchen 1278, Schivelbein 'um 1292', Dramburg 1297; before the mid-13th century the Piast dukes of Greater Poland and Silesia and the Pomeranian Griffins competed for the area. The English page: 'The Santok castellany was granted by Greater Poland's Duke Przemysł I as a dowry' (no year). Confidence 1 stays: the year is Cliopatria's, not a page's.

region.text: the western Pomeranian side of the Neumark that Cliopatria's 1272 outline adds (the 17 cells that lie inside its Holy Roman Empire Minor States shape of 1271)

ledger.note: 1272: the other 17 cells of the Neumark step, in the north (Pomeranian lands: the page's 'Pomeranian Griffins' competed with the Piasts for the area; Dramburg 1297, Schivelbein 'um 1292'). The holy-roman-empire-minor-states dossier books these 17 cells as its loss to Brandenburg in 1272, which is why the counterpart is that lump and not duchy-of-pomerania (a dossier that does not yet exist). No page gives 1272; confidence 1.

region.text: Deutsch Krone (Wałcz) and the lands round it

ledger.note: 1296: Brandenburg annexes Deutsch Krone. 'Brandenburg annexed the Międzyrzecz castellany from Greater Poland in 1297, and Deutsch Krone in 1296.' The page does not name the previous holder of Deutsch Krone; Greater Poland is the page's neighbour in the sentence. The German Neumark (Landschaft) page dates Dramburg 1297 and Schivelbein 'um 1292' (see the 1272 events).

region.text: the Międzyrzecz (Meseritz) castellany

ledger.note: 1297: Brandenburg annexes the Międzyrzecz castellany from Greater Poland. 'Brandenburg annexed the Międzyrzecz castellany from Greater Poland in 1297.' Cliopatria draws the 3 cells only from 1305.

region.text: Lower Lusatia, 'ruled by the Wettins until in 1303 it was acquired by the Ascanian margraves of Brandenburg'

ledger.note: 1303: the Ascanian margraves acquire Lower Lusatia from the Wettins. The Waldemar page dates a cession to 1312 ('Frederick of Meissen had to cede the March of Lusatia as well as the towns of Torgau and Großenhain to Brandenburg'); the two are not reconciled, and Torgau and Großenhain are not drawn.

region.text: the lands of Pomerelia, held at strategic places 'up to Gdańsk'

ledger.note: 1307: Waldemar takes Pomerelia in hand. 'In 1307 Waldemar signed an agreement with the Swienca family ceding him the lands of Pomerelia'; Brandenburg troops held strategic places 'up to Gdańsk'. Counterpart 'nobody': the ceding party is a noble family, and a Polish or Order claim is not on the page. The page names places, not a border, so the region (the gazetteer's whole Pomerelia) overstates it; the keyframes do not draw it.

region.text: Pomerelia east of the Łeba, relinquished to the Order

ledger.note: 1309-09-13: by the Treaty of Soldin Brandenburg gives up Pomerelia to the Teutonic Order. The treaty 'was signed on 13 September 1309 at Soldin (Myślibórz)'; the Order bought the rights 'for 10,000 silver Mark'; it had taken Danzig 'from the Brandenburgians' after a siege (no year on the page). The Waldemar page: Waldemar 'relinquished his claims on Pomerelia east of the Łeba River'. Not drawn in the keyframes.

region.text: Dresden

ledger.note: 1316: Waldemar occupies Dresden again. 'In 1316, Waldemar again occupied Dresden until the feud with Meissen was finally brought to an end in 1317.'

region.text: Dresden

ledger.note: 1317: the feud with Meissen ends and Dresden is no longer occupied. The page gives no treaty or month and does not say what happened to Torgau and Großenhain.

region.text: Stargard and Neubrandenburg

ledger.note: 1317: Waldemar surrenders Stargard and Neubrandenburg. 'According to the 1317 Treaty of Templin, the margrave had to surrender Stargard and Neubrandenburg to Mecklenburg.' When Brandenburg took the land is on no page opened: the Lordship of Stargard page has only the 1316 fight at Gransee 'over rights to the Lordship' and is silent on Templin. In no Cliopatria outline, so not drawn in the keyframes.

region.text: Schlawe (Sławno) and Stolp (Słupsk)

ledger.note: 1317: Waldemar waives Schlawe and Stolp. He 'had to waive the previous Pomerelian acquisitions of Schlawe and Stolp', 'which passed to Duke Wartislaw IV of Pomerania' (Waldemar page). The Wartislaw IV page says he 'received the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp as a fief from Margrave Waldemar' in 1317, so the land may have gone to him as a vassal; the year Brandenburg got it is on neither page. In no Cliopatria outline, so not drawn in the keyframes.

region.text: the Silesian towns of Züllichau and Schwiebus

ledger.note: 1319: Waldemar acquires Züllichau and Schwiebus. 'In 1319 Waldemar acquired the Silesian towns of Züllichau and Schwiebus.' The page says 'Silesian' only; Głogów is my reading of the seller (Cliopatria's row ends 1313). Region corrected in the repair to a 20 km disc round both towns: Züllichau is in no Cliopatria outline, and the ten cells that the 1314 outline adds to 1305 are the Lubusz Land (Rzepin, Torzym, Sulęcin, Międzyrzecz, one cell by Schwiebus), which the Margraviate page treats as Brandenburg's before the 1319-1322 interregnum. The disc is drawn from 1319 in the keyframes.

region.text: 'the southern portion of Lower Lusatia with the towns of Żary and Komorów Zły'

ledger.note: 1319: the south of Lower Lusatia goes to the Duchy of Jawor. 'In 1319, the southern portion of Lower Lusatia with the towns of Żary and Komorów Zły' went to Jawor (page, wording of the extraction); Gubin 'eventually fell to the Dukes of Saxe-Wittenberg'. The disc around Żary is an approximation of 'the southern portion'. Northern Lower Lusatia: see the separate 1319 loss to Saxe-Wittenberg and the 1324 return.

region.text: the northern part of Lower Lusatia (Gubin)

ledger.note: 1319: northern Lower Lusatia leaves Brandenburg's hands. 'In the northern part, in 1319, Gubin was unsuccessfully besieged by King John of Bohemia, and eventually fell to the Dukes of Saxe-Wittenberg.' The page does not date the fall, so 1319 (the siege) is the earliest year; Saxe-Wittenberg is the Ascanian line of Rudolf I, whose lands house-of-ascania covers. It returns in 1324.

region.text: the western lands round Bautzen

ledger.note: 1319: the Bohemian king takes western Upper Lusatia. 'After the extinction of the Ascanian dynasty in 1319' the neighbours claimed Upper Lusatia; 'The Bohemian king again received the western lands around Bautzen in 1319.' The 30 km disc round Bautzen is my reading of 'the western lands'.

region.text: the eastern part with Görlitz, Zittau and Lubań

ledger.note: 1319: eastern Upper Lusatia passes to the Duchy of Jawor. 'The eastern part with Görlitz, Zittau and Lubań passed to the Duchy of Jawor'; in 1329 Henry I of Jawor 'had to cede Görlitz to the Bohemian king'. The page gives the eastern part no year of its own, only the context of the Ascanian extinction of 1319.

region.text: the New March (the Neumark) with Torzym Land, without the Torzym-Sulęcin cells that go to Jawor in 1320

ledger.note: 1319: Wartislaw IV of Pomerania takes the New March. 'In 1319, Wartislaw IV of Pomerania took control of the New March with Torzym Land' (Margraviate page, 'Succession conflict after 1319'); the Lubusz Land page: 'In 1319, the region was captured by Wartislaw IV, Duke of Pomerania'. Pomerania and Saxe-Wittenberg fought 'around Küstrin in 1322–1323' and made peace in December 1323, when 'various portions of the margraviate were still controlled by various neighbouring principalities'. No page opened says when the New March came back: the 1326 gain is a bridge. Booked as a loss and a return, not as an occupation, because the schema's occupation events are written from the occupier's side. Henry II of Mecklenburg, Rudolf I of Saxe-Wittenberg and Otto the Mild of Brunswick-Lüneburg also took parts that year; not entered.

region.text: the Torzym-Sulęcin side of the Lubusz Land: 'a large portion of the Lubusz Land passed to Duke Henry I of Jawor'

ledger.note: 1320: a large portion of the Lubusz Land passes to Henry I of Jawor. 'a large portion of the Lubusz Land passed to Duke Henry I of Jawor' 'who tried to reclaim it as a region lost by his grandfather' (Margraviate page; the author's first version said only 'part'). The page names no towns for Jawor's portion: the eight Rzepin-Torzym-Sulęcin cells of the 1314 delta (less the Międzyrzecz cell, which is the 1322 event, and the Schwiebus-side cell, which is the 1319 purchase) stand for it (reading, hence confidence 2). By February 1322 'the eastern outskirts of the Lubusz Land with Torzym and Sulęcin' were controlled by Henry IV the Faithful of Żagań (same page; the Lubusz Land page: 'by 1322'). The return in 1326 is a bridge.

region.text: the Międzyrzecz castellany: the three cells of /ledger 1297 plus the Międzyrzecz town cell

ledger.note: 1322: Henry IV of Żagań holds the Międzyrzecz castellany. 'By February 1322' Torzym and Sulęcin and the Międzyrzecz castellany were controlled by 'Duke Henry IV the Faithful of Żagań'; the castellany, which Brandenburg annexed in 1297, 'was ultimately reintegrated with Poland' (undated, after the 1326 invasion of Frankfurt (Oder)). Unlike Torzym and Sulęcin it is not shown as coming back. Counterpart: Henry IV's Duchy of Żagań, a Głogów-line duchy (Cliopatria's Głogów row ends 1313); Poland is the final holder. Region: the three cells of the 1297 gain plus the town cell that Cliopatria draws from 1314. The year is the page's bound ('by February 1322'), not a date of seizure.

1323: Emperor Louis IV gives Brandenburg to his son Louis I; the Wittelsbach era begins. 'In 1323, Emperor Louis IV granted Brandenburg to his son Louis I.' The Ascanian line had died out in 1320 (Henry II, July 1320, Waldemar page); the Louis IV page gives 1323 in its text and 1324 in a cited title.

region.text: the northern part of Lower Lusatia

ledger.note: 1324: northern Lower Lusatia passes to the Wittelsbach margraves. 'In 1324, the northern part passed to the House of Wittelsbach.' The page does not say from whom; Saxe-Wittenberg is the holder its Gubin sentence names (see the 1319 loss).

region.text: the New March, back from Pomerania

ledger.note: 1326: the New March is bridged back to Brandenburg. No page opened dates the recovery. Wartislaw IV died on '1 August 1326' (Wartislaw IV page), and the Margraviate page has Bavarian forces gradually taking control of the margraviate after the 1325 interdict; its 1328-1333 war with Pomerania may mean a slower recovery. Bridge, confidence 1. From 1326 the keyframes follow Cliopatria's outlines again.

region.text: the Torzym-Sulęcin cells of the Lubusz Land

ledger.note: 1326: the Torzym-Sulęcin cells are bridged back. No page opened says when the Lubusz Land returned; the last holder the pages name is Henry IV of Żagań (1322). Brandenburg held the Neumark again by the 1402 pawn (Neumark page), and the Lubusz Land page has the Luxembourgs selling 'the region' to the Teutonic Knights. Bridge at the date of the New March bridge, confidence 1.
1356: the Golden Bull makes Brandenburg an electorate. Infobox 'Raised to electorate: 25 December 1356'; 'The Golden Bull of 1356 made Brandenburg an electorate with a vote in choosing the emperor.'

region.text: the northern part of Lower Lusatia that stayed with Brandenburg after 1319 (the page: 'In 1324, the northern part passed to the House of Wittelsbach'), drawn as Lower Lusatia without a 45 km disc around Żary

ledger.note: 1367: Otto V sells Lower Lusatia to Charles IV. Margraviate page: 'He sold Lower Lusatia, which he had already pledged to the Wettin dynasty, to Emperor Charles IV in 1367'; the Lower Lusatia page: 'In 1367 Elector Otto V sold it to Emperor Charles IV of Luxembourg' and Charles 'incorporated Lower Lusatia into the Bohemian Crown'. The sale is confirmed by both pages, so 1367 stays at confidence 3. Disagreement left open: the Wettin pledge is undated on the Margraviate page and the Lower Lusatia page says 'From 1364, entire Lower Lusatia was ruled by the Duchy of Jawor-Świdnica', so Brandenburg's effective control may have ended in 1364; the keyframes keep the northern part until the sale year because the sale is the only dated Brandenburg act.

region.text: Deutsch Krone and the lands round it

ledger.note: 1368: Casimir the Great takes Deutsch Krone. 'In 1368, Otto lost Deutsch Krone to Casimir the Great.'

1373: Charles IV buys Brandenburg for 500,000 guilders and the Luxembourg era begins. 'In 1373, Charles IV bought Brandenburg from Otto for 500,000 guilders. At the Landtag in Guben, Brandenburg was attached to the Crown of Bohemia.'

region.text: the Neumark, which 'Brandenburg pawned ... to the Teutonic Knights in 1402'

ledger.note: 1402: the Luxembourgs pawn the Neumark to the Teutonic Order. 'Brandenburg pawned the Neumark to the Teutonic Knights in 1402'; the Margraviate page: 'In 1402, an agreement with Poland allowed it to reincorporate the New March. In the same year, the Luxembourgs pawned the region to the Teutonic Knights.' The Order held it completely from 1429; Brandenburg got it back in 1454/1455.
1411: Frederick of Nuremberg, a Hohenzollern, is granted hereditary control of Brandenburg. 'In 1411, Frederick was granted hereditary control over Brandenburg.'

region.text: the Mark Brandenburg with the Altmark and the Züllichau-Schwiebus disc, without the pawned Neumark and the lost Międzyrzecz castellany

ledger.note: 1414: the estates swear allegiance to Frederick of Hohenzollern at Tangermünde, 20 March 1414; the state goes on as the Electorate of Brandenburg (electorate-of-brandenburg dossier from 1415, when Frederick is recognised as margrave and elector at Constance). This dossier ends here only because Cliopatria's row does.

wars.name: Waldemar's Pomerelian venture and the Treaty of Soldin

zones.text: Pomerelia east of the Łeba, where Brandenburg held strategic places 1307-1309

wars.outcome: 'In 1307 Waldemar signed an agreement with the Swienca family ceding him the lands of Pomerelia'; Brandenburg troops held strategic places 'up to Gdańsk'; by the 1309 Treaty of Soldin he 'relinquished his claims on Pomerelia east of the Łeba River to the Teutonic Order for a payment of 10,000' silver marks. The treaty 'was signed on 13 September 1309 at Soldin (Myślibórz)' (Treaty of Soldin page).
wars.note: Entered in the ledger in the repair as a 1307 gain and a 1309-09 loss; both lie outside every keyframe because the pages name places, not a border. The Treaty of Soldin page adds that the Order had taken Danzig 'from the Brandenburgians' after a siege (no year) and paid '10,000 silver Mark'; it does not mention Schlawe and Stolp.

wars.name: Brandenburg-Meissen feud over Lusatia and Dresden
wars.outcome: 1312: Frederick of Meissen cedes 'the March of Lusatia as well as the towns of Torgau and Großenhain'; 1316: Waldemar 'again occupied Dresden until the feud with Meissen was finally brought to an end in 1317'.
wars.note: The page gives no start of the feud and no terms for 1317. Torgau and Großenhain are not drawn.

wars.name: Waldemar's war with Mecklenburg and Pomerania (Gransee 1316, Treaty of Templin 1317)

zones.text: Stargard and Neubrandenburg, surrendered to Mecklenburg in 1317

wars.outcome: 'In August 1316, Waldemar's troops were defeated near Gransee'; by the 1317 Treaty of Templin 'the margrave had to surrender Stargard and Neubrandenburg to Mecklenburg' and waive Schlawe and Stolp, which passed to Duke Wartislaw IV of Pomerania.
wars.note: Stargard and Neubrandenburg (to Mecklenburg) and Schlawe and Stolp (to Wartislaw IV) are entered as 1317 losses in the repair; they lie outside every Cliopatria outline and are not drawn in the keyframes. The Wartislaw IV page says he 'received the Lands of Schlawe and Stolp as a fief from Margrave Waldemar' in 1317.

wars.name: Brandenburg succession conflict after the Ascanian extinction

zones.text: the New March, taken by Wartislaw IV in 1319
the Torzym-Sulęcin side of the Lubusz Land, Jawor 1320 and Żagań by February 1322
the Międzyrzecz castellany, Żagań by February 1322, later Poland

wars.outcome: After the extinction of the Ascanian line neighbours seized the margraviate piecemeal: Pomerania the New March (1319), Jawor and then Żagań the Lubusz Land (1320-1322), Saxe-Wittenberg the north of Lower Lusatia and parts of the Uckermark; Pomerania and Saxe-Wittenberg made peace in December 1323 after the fights round Küstrin; Louis IV granted Brandenburg to his son in 1323 and the neighbours cooperated against him; the Międzyrzecz castellany was 'ultimately reintegrated with Poland'.
wars.note: Added in the repair. The page dates no recovery; the ledger bridges the return of the New March and the Torzym-Sulęcin cells at 1326 (confidence 1). The page also has Mecklenburg taking Prignitz and the Uckermark, Saxe-Wittenberg the central lands and Brunswick-Lüneburg the Old March; those regions are not entered.

wars.name: Polish invasion of Frankfurt (Oder)
wars.outcome: 'In 1326, Polish King Władysław I invaded Frankfurt (Oder).' The page gives no result and no change of border.

wars.name: Louis I's war with Pomerania
wars.outcome: 'From 1328 to 1333, Louis fought Pomerania.' The page states no outcome and no land.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a survey or treaty line for the Mark; the Oder-side frontier, the Neumark and the Lusatian edge are Cliopatria's approximations, and the lump-and-correct work of 1326-1384 rests on its outlines. The treaties of Soldin (1309) and Templin (1317) fixed lines outside every drawn outline.

notes:
SAME STATE AS electorate-of-brandenburg. The Margraviate (1260-1414) and Electorate (1422-1618) rows share Wikidata Q148499 and the article 'Margraviate of Brandenburg': one state, an electorate since 25 December 1356 on the page and under Hohenzollern margraves from 1411-1415. The brief says one dossier under the earlier slug with both Names; the electorate-of-brandenburg dossier already exists (another batch) and names this one as predecessor, so this dossier covers 1260-1414 only and the orchestrator should merge or link them and give them one colour. Cliopatria's Electorate row starts 1422, so 1415-1421 is drawn by no row (the existing dossier fills it).

THE BAVARIAN LUMP. Cliopatria's shapes for 1326-1332 (77.8 k km2) and 1333-1351 (80.4-80.5 k km2) are the Mark of 1314 plus Louis IV's Bavarian lands: with Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria 1305 outline removed, the 1326 shape is the 1314 outline less six central-Altmark cells, and with the 1450 outline removed the 1333/1344 shapes are the 1314 outline less 8 Altmark cells plus 9 cells south-east of Berlin. Cliopatria then has NO Margraviate shape for 1352-1384, drawing the Mark inside its Duchy of Bavaria row (187-189 of the 196 cells of the 1314 outline for 1352-1384); the duchy-of-bavaria dossier removes it from there, and this dossier adds the new keyframes 1352 and 1368. All four were done on cell counts and on the pages opened, not on a source that states the lump.

OTHER SHAPE ERRORS FOUND. (1) The 1272 outline contains Deutsch Krone 24 years before the page's 1296. (2) [revised in the 2026-10-25 repair] The 1314 outline's 10 added cells are the Lubusz Land (Rzepin, Torzym, Sulęcin, Międzyrzecz, one cell by Schwiebus), which the Margraviate page treats as Brandenburg's before the 1319-1322 interregnum, so the outline stands from 1314; Züllichau (15.6 E) is in no outline and is added as a 20 km disc from 1319. (3) Lower Lusatia is in no outline although the page dates it 1303-1367 (partly lost 1319). (4) From 1326 every outline lacks the central and eastern Altmark (Stendal, Tangermünde, Gardelegen: 6-8 cells in 1326-1351, the whole of it in 1385-1414), although the 1260-1325 outlines have it; the Altmark is added back from 1326. (5) The 1402 outline removes only the north-east of the Neumark; the whole Neumark is removed 1402-1414 on the pawn. The existing electorate-of-brandenburg dossier says Cliopatria adds the central Altmark only in 1572 (the grid agrees that it is missing, and finds it missing from 1326) and that the Neumark is absent from the Electorate shapes of 1422-1454; in this row the 1402-1414 outlines still hold Landsberg, Küstrin and Soldin. A gap-filler should reconcile the two dossiers at 1415.

STILL NOT ENTERED (after the repair). Torgau and Großenhain (1312, undated end); the 1351 transfer of the Mark between the Wittelsbach half-brothers (keyframes only); the 1319 seizures by Mecklenburg (Prignitz, Uckermark), Saxe-Wittenberg (central lands, western Lubusz Land) and Brunswick-Lüneburg (Old March), which the page names without dated region-level sentences (the Mark west of the Oder is left whole); the Wettin pledge of Lower Lusatia (undated). Tyrol (1342) and Holland (1345) belong to the Bavarian and Dutch dossiers. No ruler strip: the Margraviate page lists only the first and last rulers. Pre-1260 history (from 1157; the Northern March and Lutician lands are the infobox's predecessors) is outside this group's period and left to an earlier-period dossier.

CONFLICTS. Lower Lusatia: 1303 (Lower Lusatia page) against 1312 (Waldemar page); 1323 against 1324 for the Wittelsbach grant (Louis IV page). The Lower Lusatia page names 'Elector Otto V' without calling him a margrave of Brandenburg; the Margraviate page names the same sale, so the identification is safe.

REGIONS: the gazetteer lacks Altmark, Lower Lusatia, Upper Lusatia and Neumark (used in corrections and events); Dresden and the disc forms resolve. Counterparts without a dossier: knights-templar, mecklenburg, duchy-of-pomerania, lower-lusatia (a state in its own right, 1303-1367 here), duchy-of-jawor (a Cliopatria row, 1279-1313, whose later history is the Jawor-Świdnica dukedom).

REPAIR 2026-10-25 (reviewer's fail verdict). Applied: (1) a 1322 loss of the Międzyrzecz castellany to the Żagań line and its removal from every keyframe from 1322; (2) a 1319 loss and a 1324 gain of northern Lower Lusatia (house-of-ascania), with the 1319-1323 keyframes without it; (3) the 1319 gain region changed to a 20 km disc round Züllichau and Schwiebus and the 1314 outline allowed to stand from 1314; (4) the 1367 note now carries the Wettin pledge and the 1364 Jawor-Świdnica rule; (5) the 1319 loss of the New March to Wartislaw IV and the 1320 loss of the Torzym-Sulęcin cells to Henry I of Jawor, each with a bridged return in 1326 (confidence 1); (6) wars: 'mecklenburg' as a slug. Also from the thin list: Upper Lusatia (gain 1262 at confidence 1, losses 1319), Pomerelia (1307, 1309-09), Stargard and Schlawe-Stolp (1317), and the 1272 Neumark step split between Greater Poland and the HRE lump. DISAGREED: (a) the 1319 Lubusz and New March losses are booked as loss plus bridged gain, not occupation_start/end, because the schema writes occupation events from the occupier's side and no page dates the return; (b) the northern Lower Lusatia loss is dated 1319 at the reviewer's confidence 2, but the Lower Lusatia page dates only the Gubin siege (1319) and says Gubin 'eventually fell' to Saxe-Wittenberg, so the fall may lie between 1319 and 1324; (c) 1364 is not used as the end of Brandenburg's Lower Lusatia (optional in the review): the Lower Lusatia page's 'From 1364, entire Lower Lusatia was ruled by the Duchy of Jawor-Świdnica' and the undated Wettin pledge are noted at the 1367 sale instead. NOT RESOLVED: the 9 cells south-east of Berlin (neither the Storkow nor the Beeskow town cell lies in any outline; the German Herrschaft Beeskow-Storkow page returned url_not_found; the Storkow and Beeskow pages are silent on a Brandenburg tenure before 1415); 1157-1259 (no dossier; outside the group's period); the counterpart duchy-of-zagan has no dossier.
